title: Expanded ten-epoch SGD learning-rate search inside heterogeneous IBM OM cell bounds
hypothesis: The original SGD search stopped at a monotonically improving boundary. Extending zero-momentum layerwise SGD geometrically to W1 in {0.512,1.024,2.048,4.096} and W2 in {0.02,0.04,0.08} will produce at least 96.0% selected validation accuracy within ten epochs from the fixed per-cell OM-bounds uniform initialization, reducing the prior 1.94-percentage-point Adam-versus-SGD validation gap by at least 1.18 percentage points.
motivation: In the completed optimizer-reference study, validation accuracy and mean cost improved monotonically across every tested W1 rate through 0.512 and every tested W2 rate through 0.02. The selected SGD arm reached 94.82% validation and 95.33% test accuracy, whereas Adam reached 96.76% validation and 96.94% test accuracy. Because the original SGD optimum lay on both search boundaries, that difference cannot yet be attributed cleanly to optimizer choice. This successor retains the exact array-specific FP32 oracle, initialization, seed, data order, architecture, and ten-epoch budget while extending only the two fixed SGD rates.

completion_criteria: Every train arm uses the exact repaired IBM OM assignment seed 84001 population with SHA-256 7e0bcfb76a0a613f0ba319786a39fdb540cce0a74f15d9fb007426a46ad49d2f and fingerprint 4887ad89abdd16193448c54a0cbe97be915cb4b9bc04cf1151c5e2a96ee5a3ac.

Every arm uses seed 17 and the same deterministic independent per-cell U[L_i,U_i] initialization, where L_i=clamp((min_bound_i-reference_i+1)/2,0,1) and U_i=clamp((max_bound_i-reference_i+1)/2,0,1). The aggregate initial-weight SHA-256 must match d8b66130f9eaad501ce78dfece8dc62acb245837517ea7c59efd18a96495f26e.

Every optimizer step is ordinary zero-momentum, zero-weight-decay digital SGD followed by exact per-cell projection to [L_i,U_i]. No pulse model, read noise, endpoint noise, quantizer, physical state evolution, or program-and-verify operation is used.

All twelve training arms use the identical bias-free [1568,100,20] perfect-diode DRN, input gain 100, voltage/current amplification 4/0.25, four forward and backward solver iterations, paired squared-error BPTT, seed-17 MNIST split/order, batch size 16, ten epochs, and exactly 34,380 optimizer minibatches.
The twelve candidates are the Cartesian product W1 in {0.512,1.024,2.048,4.096} and W2 in {0.02,0.04,0.08}. No learning-rate schedule, momentum, weight decay, warmup, or early termination is used.

Within each arm retain the earliest checkpoint with the lowest validation mean paired-squared-error cost. After all twelve development arms complete, freeze the single winner by lowest selected validation cost, breaking exact ties by higher validation accuracy and then lexicographically smaller learning-rate tuple.

Before test access, write a selection receipt containing every development run ID, selected and terminal validation metrics, config hash, initial-weight hash, and selected checkpoint hash. Evaluate only the frozen winner once on all 10,000 untouched MNIST test examples.

The fresh [0.512,0.02] anchor must reproduce the earlier arm's initial hash and selected validation metrics under the current source. The prior Adam [0.001,0.001] result is an immutable descriptive comparator: 96.76% selected validation, validation cost 0.04886919779479504, and 96.94% test accuracy.
Do not add rates, extend the ten-epoch horizon, use test results for selection, or reinterpret this hidden-bounds FP32 oracle as physical or transferable OM training after observing trajectories.
analysis_plan: Verify exact config isolation, pinned population identity, byte-identical initialization and data order, complete epoch/minibatch/example coverage, finite optimizer state, exact SGD hyperparameters, all selected weights within their own [L_i,U_i], and checkpoint hashes.

Tabulate every arm's selected epoch, selected and terminal validation accuracy/cost, projection pressure, exact rail occupancy, and final per-layer conductance and logical-contrast statistics as a two-dimensional learning-rate response surface.
Compare the fresh anchor to its earlier deterministic run and report whether the new winner is interior or remains on either grid boundary.

Report the new winner's validation and full-test differences from the original SGD winner (94.82% validation,95.33% test) and the frozen Adam winner (96.76% validation,96.94% test). Separate learning-rate under-tuning from the remaining optimizer-specific gap.
Use the better ten-epoch clean result only as an array-specific hidden-bounds FP32 ceiling for a separately declared physical pulse-training study.
